i18n.en: And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yisra'el came out of the land of Mitzrayim, in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, of Shelomoh's reign over Yisra'el, that he built the house for YHWH.

notes.official:
Names in this chapter: Yisra'el = Israel; Mitzrayim = Egypt; Shelomoh = Solomon; Ziv = Ziv (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *ṣ* is written *tz* in Kings (Mitzrayim, Tzidon, Tzadoq); genesis-woh and exodus-woh write Mitsrayim.

*bišmônîm šānâ wəʾarbaʿ mēʾôṯ šānâ* 'in the four hundred and eightieth year'. The MT figure is kept; the LXX reads 'four hundred and fortieth' and follows the verse with 6:1a–d, which carry the material of MT 5:31–32 and 6:37–38 (Rahlfs, 3 Kgdms 6:1a–d) (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). 480 is widely read as a schematic figure, twelve generations of forty years from the exodus to the Temple (Noth; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10, 2001), and it should not be used as a chronological datum without that caveat.

*bəḥōḏeš ziw hûʾ haḥōḏeš haššēnî* 'in the month of Ziv, which is the second month'. Ziv (6:1, 37), Bul (6:38) and Etanim (8:2) are old Canaanite month names, glossed in the text by the later ordinal months; Bul is attested in Phoenician (Eshmunazar sarcophagus, KAI 14:1). Ziv corresponds to the later Iyyar (April-May). The names are transliterated, as in the ASV.

*wayyiḇen habbayiṯ* 'that he built the house'. The ASV 'began to build' interprets the verb by 6:37-38, where the work takes seven years; the Hebrew has the plain wayyiqtol, which can carry an ingressive sense, and the line keeps the plain verb.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) summarises chs. 6-8 by saying that Shelomoh built 'a sumptuous residence to receive the creators when they came on a visit'. The translation renders *bayiṯ* 'house' as all versions do; the reception reading is recorded here only.

i18n.en: And the house which King Shelomoh built for YHWH: sixty cubits was its length, and twenty its breadth, and thirty cubits its height.

notes.official: *habbayiṯ* 'the house' is the whole building; its main room is the *hêḵāl* and its rear room the *dəḇîr* (vv 3, 5, 16-17; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *šiššîm-ʾammâ ʾorkô* 'sixty cubits was its length'. The *ʾammâ* 'cubit' (forearm length) is kept as in all versions; the common cubit is about 44-45 cm, and 2 Chr 3:3 specifies cubits 'of the old standard', usually taken as the longer royal cubit of about 52 cm. The interior is then roughly 27-31 m by 9-10 m by 13-16 m. The long-room plan with porch, hall and rear shrine has close Iron Age parallels in north Syria, notably the temples of ʿAin Dara and Tell Tayinat (Monson, *BAR* 26/3, 2000; King and Stager, *Life in Biblical Israel*, 2001).

paragraphs.text: וְהָאוּלָ֗ם עַל־פְּנֵי֙ הֵיכַ֣ל הַבַּ֔יִת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רֹ֣חַב הַבָּ֑יִת עֶ֧שֶׂר בָּאַמָּ֛ה רָחְבּ֖וֹ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: And the porch in front of the great hall of the house: twenty cubits was its length, along the breadth of the house; ten cubits was its breadth in front of the house.

notes.official:
*wəhāʾûlām ʿal-pənê hêḵal habbayiṯ* 'And the porch in front of the great hall of the house' (ASV 'the temple of the house'). *hêḵāl* is a loanword from Sumerian é.gal 'great house' (via Akkadian *ekallu*), meaning 'palace' or 'temple' in general and, in the Temple plan, the large main room between the *ʾûlām* and the *dəḇîr* (HALOT *hêḵāl* 3). The ASV 'temple' gives the general sense, but in this chapter the whole building is *bayiṯ* 'house', so 'temple' for one of its rooms would mislead; 'great hall' follows NJPS and Alter (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *ʾûlām* 'porch' (ASV; NJPS 'portico', NRSV 'vestibule') is kept.

*ʿeśer bāʾammâ rāḥbô* 'ten cubits was its breadth': the distributive *bāʾammâ* 'by the cubit' (also vv 6, 17, 25, 26) is rendered simply 'cubits'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לַבָּ֔יִת חַלּוֹנֵ֖י שְׁקֻפִ֥ים אֲטֻמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And for the house he made windows of fixed lattice-work.

notes.official: *ḥallônê šəqūp̄îm ʾăṭūmîm* 'windows of fixed lattice-work' (ASV). Both modifiers are technical and uncertain: *šəqūp̄îm* is related to *šqp* 'look down / frame', and *ʾăṭūmîm* to *ʾṭm* 'close, stop up'. Proposals include 'windows with recessed frames' (NRSV), 'windows, recessed and latticed' (NJPS) and narrow, splayed clerestory openings (Busink, *Der Tempel von Jerusalem*, 1970; Cogan). The ASV wording is kept as one defensible reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבֶן֩ עַל־קִ֨יר הַבַּ֤יִת יצוע [יָצִ֙יעַ֙] סָבִ֔יב אֶת־קִיר֤וֹת הַבַּ֙יִת֙ סָבִ֔יב לַֽהֵיכָ֖ל וְלַדְּבִ֑יר וַיַּ֥עַשׂ צְלָע֖וֹת סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: And against the wall of the house he built stories all around, against the walls of the house all around, of both the great hall and the inner sanctuary; and he made side-chambers all around.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *yṣwʿ* (vocalized as *yāṣûaʿ* 'couch, bed') / Qere *yāṣîaʿ* 'side-structure'; the Qere is translated, here and at vv 6, 10 (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*wayyiḇen ʿal-qîr habbayiṯ yāṣîaʿ sāḇîḇ* 'And against the wall of the house he built stories all around' (ASV). *yāṣîaʿ* is the multi-storey annex built against three sides of the building (HALOT 'side-building, lean-to'); *ṣəlāʿôṯ* (lit. 'ribs, sides') are its 'side-chambers'. The ASV 'stories' is kept because v 6 describes the annex by its three levels. *lahêḵāl wəladdəḇîr* 'of both the great hall and the inner sanctuary' (ASV 'temple ... oracle'; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: היצוע [הַיָּצִ֨יעַ] הַתַּחְתֹּנָ֜ה חָמֵ֧שׁ בָּאַמָּ֣ה רָחְבָּ֗הּ וְהַתִּֽיכֹנָה֙ שֵׁ֤שׁ בָּֽאַמָּה֙ רָחְבָּ֔הּ וְהַ֨שְּׁלִישִׁ֔ית שֶׁ֥בַע בָּאַמָּ֖ה רָחְבָּ֑הּ כִּ֡י מִגְרָעוֹת֩ נָתַ֨ן לַבַּ֤יִת סָבִיב֙ ח֔וּצָה לְבִלְתִּ֖י אֲחֹ֥ז בְּקִֽירוֹת־הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: The lowest story was five cubits in breadth, and the middle one six cubits in breadth, and the third seven cubits in breadth; for he made offsets for the house all around on the outside, so that nothing should take hold in the walls of the house.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *hyṣwʿ* / Qere *hayyāṣîaʿ* 'the side-structure' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`); the line reads 'The lowest story'.

*kî miḡrāʿôṯ nāṯan labbayiṯ* 'for he made offsets for the house': the wall of the main building was stepped back by one cubit at each level (*miḡrāʿôṯ* 'recesses, rebatements', from *grʿ* 'reduce'), so that the joists of each storey rested on a ledge and were not set into the wall itself (*ləḇiltî ʾăḥōz bəqîrôṯ-habbāyiṯ*), which explains the growing widths of five, six and seven cubits (Cogan; Gray, *I & II Kings*, OTL).

paragraphs.text: וְהַבַּ֙יִת֙ בְּהִבָּ֣נֹת֔וֹ אֶֽבֶן־שְׁלֵמָ֥ה מַסָּ֖ע נִבְנָ֑ה וּמַקָּב֤וֹת וְהַגַּרְזֶן֙ כָּל־כְּלִ֣י בַרְזֶ֔ל לֹֽא־נִשְׁמַ֥ע בַּבַּ֖יִת בְּהִבָּנֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the house, when it was being built, was built of stone finished at the quarry; and neither hammers nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was being built.

notes.official: *ʾeḇen-šəlēmâ massāʿ* 'stone finished at the quarry' (lit. 'whole stone of the quarry'): the blocks were dressed at the quarry. The silence of tools at the building site recalls the law of the altar of unhewn stone (Ex 20:22 MT = 20:25 ASV), but the text does not draw that connection.

paragraphs.text: פֶּ֗תַח הַצֵּלָע֙ הַתִּ֣יכֹנָ֔ה אֶל־כֶּ֥תֶף הַבַּ֖יִת הַיְמָנִ֑ית וּבְלוּלִּ֗ים יַֽעֲלוּ֙ עַל־הַתִּ֣יכֹנָ֔ה וּמִן־הַתִּֽיכֹנָ֖ה אֶל־הַשְּׁלִשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: The entrance of the middle side-chamber was on the right-hand side of the house; and by winding stairs they went up into the middle story, and from the middle into the third.

notes.official:
*peṯaḥ haṣṣēlāʿ hattîḵōnâ* 'The entrance of the middle side-chamber'. The MT 'middle' is translated; the LXX reads 'the lowest', which many commentators prefer because an entrance to the annex would be expected at ground level (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

*ûḇəlûllîm yaʿălû* 'and by winding stairs they went up' (ASV). *lûllîm* occurs only here; the ASV 'winding stairs' follows the Targum and Rashi, while others propose 'trapdoors' or 'shafts' (cf. Mishnaic *lûl* 'opening, shaft', m. Middot 4:5; HALOT; Cogan). The ASV wording is kept and the alternatives are noted.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֥בֶן אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת וַיְכַלֵּ֑הוּ וַיִּסְפֹּ֤ן אֶת־הַבַּ֙יִת֙ גֵּבִ֔ים וּשְׂדֵרֹ֖ת בָּאֲרָזִֽים׃

i18n.en: So he built the house and finished it; and he covered the house with beams and planks of cedar.

notes.official: *wayyispōn ʾeṯ-habbayiṯ gēḇîm ûśəḏērōṯ bāʾărāzîm* 'and he covered the house with beams and planks of cedar'. Both nouns are rare; the ASV sense (roofing of beams and boards) is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֤בֶן אֶת־היצוע [הַיָּצִ֙יעַ֙] עַל־כָּל־הַבַּ֔יִת חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֽוֹמָת֑וֹ וַיֶּאֱחֹ֥ז אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת בַּעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִֽים׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he built the stories against the whole house, five cubits its height; and it held onto the house with timbers of cedar.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *hyṣwʿ* / Qere *hayyāṣîaʿ* 'the side-structure' (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *wayyeʾĕḥōz ʾeṯ-habbayiṯ* 'and it held onto the house': the subject is unexpressed and is best taken as the annex, attached to the main building by its cedar joists (ASV 'and they rested on the house'). The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the building report before the oracle of vv 11-13.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And the word of YHWH came to Shelomoh, saying,

notes.official: *wayəhî dəḇar-YHWH ʾel-šəlōmōh lēʾmōr* 'And the word of YHWH came to Shelomoh, saying' (`davar-yhwh-prophetic-formula`). Verses 11-14 are absent from the LXX (Vaticanus), and many critics regard them as a Deuteronomistic insertion that interrupts the building report (Noth; Cogan); the MT is translated in full (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: הַבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה בֹנֶ֗ה אִם־תֵּלֵ֤ךְ בְּחֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֣י תַּֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֥ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתַ֖י לָלֶ֣כֶת בָּהֶ֑ם וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־דְּבָרִי֙ אִתָּ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: "This house which you are building — if you walk in my statutes, and do my ordinances, and keep all my commandments to walk in them, then I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father.

notes.official: *ḥuqqōṯay ... mišpāṭay ... miṣwōṯay* 'my statutes ... my ordinances ... my commandments' (ASV). The conditional promise restates 2 Sam 7:12-16 in Deuteronomistic terms; *wahăqimōṯî ʾeṯ-dəḇārî* 'then I will establish my word' points back to the dynastic oracle to David.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁ֣כַנְתִּ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֥א אֶעֱזֹ֖ב אֶת־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra'el, and I will not forsake my people Yisra'el."

notes.official:
*wəšāḵantî bəṯôḵ bənê yiśrāʾēl* 'And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra'el'. *šāḵan* is the verb of the divine presence settling among Israel (Ex 25:8; 29:45-46), the root of *miškān* 'dwelling, tabernacle' and of the later rabbinic *šəḵînâ*; it is rendered 'dwell' as in the ASV (`shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`). *bəṯôḵ* is rendered literally 'in the midst of' (ASV 'among'), the same phrase as Ex 25:8 and 29:45. The verse belongs to the section absent from the LXX (see v 11).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('I will dwell among the children of Israel') as part of its account of the Temple as a residence for the creators. The line renders *šāḵan* and *bəṯôḵ* lexically and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֧בֶן שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־הַבַּ֖יִת וַיְכַלֵּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: So Shelomoh built the house and finished it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־קִיר֨וֹת הַבַּ֤יִת מִבַּ֙יְתָה֙ בְּצַלְע֣וֹת אֲרָזִ֔ים מִקַּרְקַ֤ע הַבַּ֙יִת֙ עַד־קִיר֣וֹת הַסִּפֻּ֔ן צִפָּ֥ה עֵ֖ץ מִבָּ֑יִת וַיְצַ֛ף אֶת־קַרְקַ֥ע הַבַּ֖יִת בְּצַלְע֥וֹת בְּרוֹשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: And he built the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling he covered them on the inside with wood; and he covered the floor of the house with boards of fir.

notes.official:
*ʿaḏ-qîrôṯ hassippun* 'to the walls of the ceiling' (MT). Many emend *qîrôṯ* 'walls' to *qôrôṯ* 'rafters, beams', with the LXX ('to the beams'), giving 'from the floor to the beams of the ceiling'; the MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

*bərôšîm* 'fir' (ASV; also v 34): the tree is a conifer from Lebanon, probably the Phoenician juniper or the cypress (Zohary, *Plants of the Bible*, 1982; NRSV 'cypress'); the ASV word is kept.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּבֶן֩ אֶת־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים אַמָּ֜ה מירכותי [מִֽיַּרְכְּתֵ֤י] הַבַּ֙יִת֙ בְּצַלְע֣וֹת אֲרָזִ֔ים מִן־הַקַּרְקַ֖ע עַד־הַקִּיר֑וֹת וַיִּ֤בֶן לוֹ֙ מִבַּ֣יִת לִדְבִ֔יר לְקֹ֖דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃

i18n.en: And he built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar, from the floor to the walls; he built it for it within, as an inner sanctuary, as the most holy place.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *myrkwty* / Qere *miyyarkəṯê* 'from the rear parts of' (orthographic; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*wayyiḇen lô mibbayiṯ liḏḇîr ləqōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* 'he built it for it within, as an inner sanctuary, as the most holy place'. *dəḇîr* is the rear room of the house (HALOT 'back room'). The ASV 'oracle' goes back to the Vulgate *oraculum* and to an old derivation from *dbr* 'speak', which modern lexica reject; the line uses 'inner sanctuary' (NRSV) throughout (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* 'the most holy place' (ASV) is the superlative construct 'holy of holies' (GKC §133i).

paragraphs.text: וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים בָּאַמָּ֖ה הָיָ֣ה הַבָּ֑יִת ה֖וּא הַהֵיכָ֥ל לִפְנָֽי׃

i18n.en: And the house, that is, the great hall in front, was forty cubits.

notes.official: *hûʾ hahêḵāl lip̄nāy* 'that is, the great hall in front'. *lip̄nāy* is a unique form; the ASV 'before [the oracle]' takes it as 'in front (of the rear room)', and some emend to *lip̄nê haddəḇîr*. The line follows the ASV sense; the forty cubits of the hall plus the twenty of the *dəḇîr* give the sixty of v 2 (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶ֤רֶז אֶל־הַבַּ֙יִת֙ פְּנִ֔ימָה מִקְלַ֣עַת פְּקָעִ֔ים וּפְטוּרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים הַכֹּ֣ל אֶ֔רֶז אֵ֥ין אֶ֖בֶן נִרְאָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the cedar on the house within was carved with gourds and open flowers; all was cedar; no stone was seen.

notes.official: *miqlaʿaṯ pəqāʿîm ûp̄əṭûrê ṣiṣṣîm* 'carved with gourds and open flowers'. *pəqāʿîm* are gourd-shaped ornaments (HALOT; cf. 7:24); the ASV 'knops' (an archaic word for 'knobs') is replaced by 'gourds' (NRSV, NJPS), which also keeps the lexical link with *paqquʿōṯ śāḏeh* 'wild gourds' at 2 Kgs 4:39 (`peqaim-gourd-ornaments-1-kings-6`). *pəṭûrê ṣiṣṣîm* 'open flowers' (ASV) and *tîmōrôṯ* 'palm-trees' (v 29) are kept.

paragraphs.text: וּדְבִ֧יר בְּתוֹךְ־הַבַּ֛יִת מִפְּנִ֖ימָה הֵכִ֑ין לְתִתֵּ֣ן שָׁ֔ם אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן בְּרִ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he prepared an inner sanctuary in the midst of the house, within, to set there the ark of the covenant of YHWH.

notes.official: *ûḏəḇîr bəṯôḵ-habbayiṯ mippənîmâ hēḵîn* 'And he prepared an inner sanctuary in the midst of the house, within' (ASV 'an oracle'; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *lattittēn šām ʾeṯ-ʾărôn bərîṯ YHWH* 'to set there the ark of the covenant of YHWH': the ark is installed in 8:6.

paragraphs.text: וְלִפְנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֡יר עֶשְׂרִים֩ אַמָּ֨ה אֹ֜רֶךְ וְעֶשְׂרִ֧ים אַמָּ֣ה רֹ֗חַב וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים אַמָּה֙ קֽוֹמָת֔וֹ וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר וַיְצַ֥ף מִזְבֵּ֖חַ אָֽרֶז׃

i18n.en: And the interior of the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in height; and he overlaid it with pure gold; and he covered the altar with cedar.

notes.official:
*wəlip̄nê haddəḇîr* 'And the interior of the inner sanctuary' (ASV 'within the oracle'). The MT literally reads 'and before the *dəḇîr*', usually explained as 'the interior of' (*pənê* 'face, inner part') or emended; the line renders that sense. The room is a perfect cube of twenty cubits, ten cubits lower than the hall (v 2), so it was raised on a platform or had a lowered ceiling (Cogan).

*zāhāḇ sāḡûr* 'pure gold' (ASV; lit. 'closed gold', perhaps 'refined'). *wayṣap̄ mizbēaḥ ʾārez* 'and he covered the altar with cedar' (MT); the LXX reads 'and he made an altar' (*wayyaʿaś*), which many prefer (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). The altar is the incense altar in front of the *dəḇîr* (v 22; 7:48).

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֨ף שְׁלֹמֹ֧ה אֶת־הַבַּ֛יִת מִפְּנִ֖ימָה זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר וַיְעַבֵּ֞ר ברתיקות [בְּרַתּוּק֤וֹת] זָהָב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֔יר וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: So Shelomoh overlaid the house within with pure gold; and he drew chains of gold across in front of the inner sanctuary; and he overlaid it with gold.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *brtyqwt* / Qere *bərattûqôṯ* 'with chains' (orthographic; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *wayʿabbēr ... lip̄nê haddəḇîr* 'and he drew chains of gold across in front of the inner sanctuary': the chains probably closed the entrance between hall and rear room (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־כָּל־הַבַּ֛יִת צִפָּ֥ה זָהָ֖ב עַד־תֹּ֣ם כָּל־הַבָּ֑יִת וְכָל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־לַדְּבִ֖יר צִפָּ֥ה זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until all the house was completed; also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.

notes.official: *wəḵol-hammizbēaḥ ʾăšer-laddəḇîr* 'also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary': the incense altar stood in the hall before the *dəḇîr* (cf. v 20; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ בַּדְּבִ֔יר שְׁנֵ֥י כְרוּבִ֖ים עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת קוֹמָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And in the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive-wood, each ten cubits high.

notes.official: *šənê ḵərûḇîm ʿăṣê-šāmen* 'two cherubim of olive-wood' (central `cherubim-ezek`, whose rationale already cites these verses; the Temple cherubim are the ones under whose wings the ark is placed at 8:6-7). *ʿăṣê-šemen* is literally 'trees of oil'; Neh 8:15 distinguishes it from the olive (*zayiṯ*), so it may be the oleaster or a resinous conifer (Zohary 1982). The ASV 'olive-wood' is kept here and at vv 31-33. The cherubim of the *dəḇîr* (inner sanctuary; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`) are free-standing figures ten cubits high, distinct from the two small cherubim on the ark's cover in Ex 25:18-20.

paragraphs.text: וְחָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֗וֹת כְּנַ֤ף הַכְּרוּב֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת וְחָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת כְּנַ֥ף הַכְּר֖וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֔וֹת מִקְצ֥וֹת כְּנָפָ֖יו וְעַד־קְצ֥וֹת כְּנָפָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And five cubits was the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the second wing of the cherub: ten cubits from the tips of its wings to the tips of its wings.

notes.official: The two wings of each cherub measure five cubits each, ten cubits from tip to tip; together the two figures span the twenty-cubit width of the room (v 27; `cherubim-ezek`).

paragraphs.text: וְעֶ֙שֶׂר֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה הַכְּר֖וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֑י מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת וְקֶ֥צֶב אֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַכְּרֻבִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the second cherub was ten cubits; both the cherubim had one measure and one form.

notes.official: *middâ ʾaḥaṯ wəqeṣeḇ ʾeḥāḏ* 'one measure and one form': *qeṣeḇ* is 'shape, cut' (cf. 7:37). `cherubim-ezek`.

paragraphs.text: קוֹמַת֙ הַכְּר֣וּב הָֽאֶחָ֔ד עֶ֖שֶׂר בָּֽאַמָּ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן הַכְּר֥וּב הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

i18n.en: The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the second cherub.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֶת־הַכְּרוּבִ֜ים בְּת֣וֹךְ ׀ הַבַּ֣יִת הַפְּנִימִ֗י וַֽיִּפְרְשׂוּ֮ אֶת־כַּנְפֵ֣י הַכְּרֻבִים֒ וַתִּגַּ֤ע כְּנַף־הָֽאֶחָד֙ בַּקִּ֔יר וּכְנַף֙ הַכְּר֣וּב הַשֵּׁנִ֔י נֹגַ֖עַת בַּקִּ֣יר הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַבַּ֔יִת נֹגְעֹ֖ת כָּנָ֥ף אֶל־כָּנָֽף׃

i18n.en: And he set the cherubim in the midst of the inner house; and the wings of the cherubim were spread out, so that the wing of the one touched the wall, and the wing of the second cherub touched the second wall; and their wings in the midst of the house touched wing to wing.

notes.official: *bəṯôḵ habbayiṯ happənîmî* 'in the midst of the inner house', the *dəḇîr*. *wayyip̄rəśû ʾeṯ-kanp̄ê hakkərūḇîm* 'and the wings of the cherubim were spread out': the verb is active plural with an indefinite subject ('they spread out'), rendered as a passive, as in the ASV. Wing touching wall and wing touching wing create the canopy under which the ark is set (8:6-7; `cherubim-ezek`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֥ף אֶת־הַכְּרוּבִ֖ים זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵת֩ כָּל־קִיר֨וֹת הַבַּ֜יִת מֵסַ֣ב ׀ קָלַ֗ע פִּתּוּחֵי֙ מִקְלְעוֹת֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים וְתִֽמֹרֹ֔ת וּפְטוּרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים מִלִּפְנִ֖ים וְלַחִיצֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And all the walls of the house all around he carved with engraved carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers, inside and outside.

notes.official: *mēsaḇ qālaʿ pittûḥê miqləʿôṯ* 'all around he carved with engraved carvings'. Cherubim, palm-trees and flowers are the standard decorative program of Phoenician-Syrian ivories and temple reliefs; the combination recurs in Ezekiel's temple (Ezek 41:18-20, 25; `cherubim-ezek`). *millip̄nîm wəlaḥîṣôn* 'inside and outside' probably means in the inner room (*dəḇîr*) and in the outer room (*hêḵāl*), not inside and outside the building (Cogan).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־קַרְקַ֥ע הַבַּ֖יִת צִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֑ב לִפְנִ֖ימָה וְלַחִיצֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, inside and outside.

notes.official: *lip̄nîmâ wəlaḥîṣôn* 'inside and outside', i.e. in the inner and the outer room (see v 29).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵת֙ פֶּ֣תַח הַדְּבִ֔יר עָשָׂ֖ה דַּלְת֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן הָאַ֥יִל מְזוּז֖וֹת חֲמִשִֽׁית׃

i18n.en: And for the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive-wood; the lintel and the doorposts were a fifth part.

notes.official: *wəʾēṯ peṯaḥ haddəḇîr* 'And for the entrance of the inner sanctuary' (ASV 'oracle'; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *hāʾayil məzûzôṯ ḥămišîṯ* 'the lintel and the doorposts were a fifth part' (ASV, which adds 'of the wall'). The phrase is a crux: *ḥămišîṯ* 'fifth' may give the proportion of the doorway to the wall, or describe a five-sided (pentagonal) frame, or a frame recessed in five stages (NRSV 'five-sided'; NJPS 'pentagonal'; Cogan). The parallel *rəḇiʿîṯ* 'fourth' at v 33 is treated the same way. The ASV construal is kept and the alternatives are recorded.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁתֵּי֮ דַּלְת֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שֶׁמֶן֒ וְקָלַ֣ע עֲ֠לֵיהֶם מִקְלְע֨וֹת כְּרוּבִ֧ים וְתִמֹר֛וֹת וּפְטוּרֵ֥י צִצִּ֖ים וְצִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֑ב וַיָּ֛רֶד עַל־הַכְּרוּבִ֥ים וְעַל־הַתִּֽמֹר֖וֹת אֶת־הַזָּהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And the two doors were of olive-wood; and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he spread the gold upon the cherubim and upon the palm-trees.

notes.official: *wayyāreḏ ... ʾeṯ-hazzāhāḇ* 'and he spread the gold' (lit. 'he made the gold go down'), i.e. hammered gold foil over the carved relief so that the figures stayed visible (`cherubim-ezek`).

paragraphs.text: וְכֵ֥ן עָשָׂ֛ה לְפֶ֥תַח הַֽהֵיכָ֖ל מְזוּז֣וֹת עֲצֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן מֵאֵ֖ת רְבִעִֽית׃

i18n.en: So also he made for the entrance of the great hall doorposts of olive-wood, a fourth part;

notes.official: *ləp̄eṯaḥ hahêḵāl* 'for the entrance of the great hall' (ASV 'the temple'; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *mēʾēṯ rəḇiʿîṯ* 'a fourth part': see v 31.

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁתֵּ֥י דַלְת֖וֹת עֲצֵ֣י בְרוֹשִׁ֑ים שְׁנֵ֨י צְלָעִ֜ים הַדֶּ֤לֶת הָֽאַחַת֙ גְּלִילִ֔ים וּשְׁנֵ֧י קְלָעִ֛ים הַדֶּ֥לֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית גְּלִילִֽים׃

i18n.en: and two doors of fir-wood: the two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the second door were folding.

notes.official: *šənê ṣəlāʿîm ... ûšənê qəlāʿîm* 'the two leaves ... and the two leaves'. In the second half the MT has *qəlāʿîm* (elsewhere 'hangings, curtains', Ex 27:9), where the first half has *ṣəlāʿîm* 'leaves'; BDB records 'leaf (of a door)' for this verse, and most commentators read *ṣəlāʿîm* in both halves. Either way the sense is 'leaves', as in the ASV, so the line does not depart from the consonantal text (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *gəlîlîm* 'folding' (lit. 'turning'). *bərôšîm* 'fir', see v 15.

paragraphs.text: וְקָלַ֤ע כְּרוּבִים֙ וְתִ֣מֹר֔וֹת וּפְטֻרֵ֖י צִצִּ֑ים וְצִפָּ֣ה זָהָ֔ב מְיֻשָּׁ֖ר עַל־הַמְּחֻקֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he carved cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold fitted evenly upon the engraved work.

notes.official: *zāhāḇ məyuššār ʿal-hamməḥuqqeh* 'gold fitted evenly upon the engraved work' (ASV 'fitted upon the graven work'): the gold foil followed the relief (cf. v 32; `cherubim-ezek`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔ית שְׁלֹשָׁ֖ה טוּרֵ֣י גָזִ֑ית וְט֖וּר כְּרֻתֹ֥ת אֲרָזִֽים׃

i18n.en: And he built the inner court with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams.

notes.official: *šəlōšâ ṭûrê ḡāzîṯ wəṭûr kəruṯōṯ ʾărāzîm* 'three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams': a building technique attested at Megiddo, Ugarit and other Late Bronze and Iron Age sites, in which a timber course is laid over several courses of ashlar (Cogan; cf. 7:12; Ezra 6:4).

paragraphs.text: בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית יֻסַּ֖ד בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּיֶ֖רַח זִֽו׃

i18n.en: In the fourth year the foundation of the house of YHWH was laid, in the month of Ziv.

notes.official: *bəyeraḥ ziw* 'in the month of Ziv'. Here and at v 38 and 8:2 the month is *yeraḥ*, the older Canaanite word (as in Phoenician), where 6:1 has *ḥōḏeš*; both are rendered 'month'. *yussaḏ* 'was laid', of the foundation.

paragraphs.text: וּבַשָּׁנָה֩ הָאַחַ֨ת עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה בְּיֶ֣רַח בּ֗וּל ה֚וּא הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י כָּלָ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְכָל־דְּבָרָ֖יו וּלְכָל־משפטו [מִשְׁפָּטָ֑יו] וַיִּבְנֵ֖הוּ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts and according to all its specifications. So he was seven years in building it.

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *mšpṭw* 'its specification' (singular) / Qere *mišpāṭāyw* 'its specifications' (plural); the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). The ASV ('according to all the fashion of it') follows the singular.

*bəyeraḥ bûl hûʾ haḥōḏeš haššəmînî* 'in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month' (later Marcheshvan, October-November). *mišpāṭ* here means the prescribed plan or design ('specifications'), not judgement or law. From Ziv of year 4 to Bul of year 11 is seven and a half years, rounded to seven.
